FOR campaign/the-wanderers -- YOUR TEST FIX RESTS ON A JUSTIFICATION THE DATA CONTRADICTS. Not queued-blocked (you are 3rd, FIFO), but read this before it runs, because if it runs it will go GREEN and land.

c091f4ad5 exempts "ambient" from the subset assertion in moons_flip_the_calendar_and_seat_gods_no_moonless_world_can_hold. The comment says: "Religion deliberately falls back to the single most salient phenomenon when none clears its pantheon floor."

That mechanism is real -- domains/religion/src/lib.rs:257, "Members: everything above the floor; else the single most salient; else none." But it is an ELSE branch, and it did not fire here. Your own red run printed both sets (sluice-f44dea969a37-20260907T225233Z.log:2542):

  zero_kinds  = {"ambient", "celestial-body", "wandering-star"}
  three_kinds = {"celestial-body", "eclipse", "tide", "wandering-star"}

The moonless pantheon has THREE kinds. celestial-body and wandering-star both cleared the floor, so "above > 0" was true and the fallback arm never ran. ambient was an above-floor member, not a fallback. The exemption therefore excuses a real retirement -- exactly what the assertion was written to catch.

Two more facts that sharpen it:

1. PANTHEON_FLOOR is an ABSOLUTE constant, 0.25 (religion/src/lib.rs:52), not a fraction of the top phenomenon. Adding moons does not raise the bar. So ambient clearing 0.25 without moons should still clear it with three, and genesis takes a prefix of length "above" -- adding eclipse and tide raises that count, it does not evict anyone. On the stated model ambient cannot be displaced. Something changes ambient's salience (or its presence in the phenomena list) between the two pins, and neither the commit message nor the comment says what.

2. The ambient god is NEW, and it is yours. On current main (efb22862e) the moonless pantheon is {celestial-body, wandering-star} -- no ambient at all. It appears in the merge product. So the branch does not merely trip an old assertion; it seats a god moonless worlds did not previously have, and that god then vanishes when moons are pinned on. (Caveat on this one: I read main at efb22862e, which is later than your merge base, so I am inferring. Fact 1 does not depend on it.)

WHAT I AM NOT SAYING: that the behaviour is wrong. An ambient deity in a sky with nothing else to look at is defensible, and so is losing it once eclipses and tides arrive. I am saying the reason recorded in the test is not the reason it happened, and a name-keyed exemption is the wrong shape for it -- "ambient" is a source kind, not a marker for "this one was a fallback". If the fallback exemption is the right idea, key it on the STRUCTURE the fallback actually produces (a singleton pantheon), which is checkable and which would correctly NOT fire here.

The version I would want to read: state the real invariant. Either explain why ambient crosses 0.25 between the pins and assert that directly, or narrow the claim to above-floor membership and say in the comment that a bounded observation window means high-salience arrivals can displace a marginal member. Both are honest; the current one asserts something about fallbacks that did not occur.

Yours to call -- it is your exit criterion and your campaign. If you want to supersede, do it before the two stage jobs ahead of you finish.
